audit.why: Four spikes present: Lvl 2 pre-dash window, Lvl 6 conditional on Mega, Graves's first item, and the Rage-fills spike. The last is a state rather than a level but it is honest and I did not invent a timing for it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says Smoke Screen 'blinds your Mini autos and Hyper'. Riot's description says it creates a cloud that reduces sight range, plus impact damage and a brief slow — no blind, no attack miss. It also never mentions that Quickdraw's cooldown is refunded by Graves's basic attacks, or that his shotgun bullets cannot pass through units.
audit.why: Three concrete consequences. You can keep attacking inside the smoke, so the advice to hold trades is built on a mechanic that does not exist. Quickdraw is not a fixed clock — every auto he lands brings the dash back sooner, so counting seconds gets Gnar killed. And because New Destiny's four bullets cannot pass through units, keeping a minion between you and Graves eats his burst outright.
audit.corrected: Smoke re-described as vision denial plus slow in wants.foe[1] and whys[2]; Quickdraw's auto-refund and 14s rank-3 cooldown added to the do's and cooldown block; the bullets-blocked-by-units rule added to Key Ability Interactions.
sources: enemyKit Graves E text 'Hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers the cooldown of this skill'
enemyKit Graves P text 'Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units'

notes: No mirror audit existed for graves__gnar; this side is the first pass. Facts to restate inverted when it is written: Gnar owns Level 2 before Quickdraw exists, Graves owns Level 3 onward and from his first item, Quickdraw's cooldown is auto-refunded, Smoke Screen denies vision rather than blinding, and New Destiny's bullets are stopped by minions. The packet defect 'never names any of Graves's abilities' is now partly closed — Quickdraw and Smoke Screen appear by name; End of the Line, New Destiny and Collateral Damage still do not, because the surviving slots for them are long prose paragraphs and a name swap alone would not justify the length-band risk.
